long.title: The Ultraviolet Catastrophe — how energy comes in chunks | Bear's Notes
long.description:
Heat any object and it glows, and physics in 1900 could predict that glow. The prediction was not "very bright" — it was infinitely bright. Taken literally, the warm walls of your room should blast you with ultraviolet light.

A Brown Blue explainer, in the 3Blue1Brown tradition: concrete before abstract, mystery before formula.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
0:20 Counting the patterns of light
0:42 The classical prediction runs away
1:00 Which step was the lie?
1:13 Planck's fix: energy in chunks
1:33 Why the catastrophe never happens
1:47 Classical vs. quantum

In this video: why counting standing-wave modes makes the classical prediction run away; where equipartition breaks; how energy in whole chunks (E = hν) bends the curve back to zero; and the ratio hν / kT that decides when quantum effects matter.

Source: Quantum Mechanics, Vol. 1, Ch. 1 — Why Classical Physics Failed.
